A Domain holds Services, a Service holds Workloads, and
every composite hangs off the Workload that declares it. Each generation
is a band, and the gap between two bands carries the connectors — which is
why none of them crosses a box." style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontFamily=Helvetica;fontSize=12;fontColor=#334155;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="2500" y="60" width="560" height="110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="t214" value="A filled diamond is composition: the part cannot exist without its whole.
A dashed arrow is a reference resolved by name, and it runs in its own
lane below the tree. Where two connectors cross, the one that hops over is
the one passing through." style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontFamily=Helvetica;fontSize=12;fontColor=#334155;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="2500" y="190" width="560" height="110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

g.text: Root at the top. A Domain holds Services, a Service holds Workloads, and
every composite hangs off the Workload that declares it. Each generation
is a band, and the gap between two bands carries the connectors — which is
why none of them crosses a box.
A filled diamond is composition: the part cannot exist without its whole.
A dashed arrow is a reference resolved by name, and it runs in its own
lane below the tree. Where two connectors cross, the one that hops over is
